conflicts.about: How the commodity search runs: in the browser as you type (DR2.1) or on the server when Search is pressed (today).

positions.says: The search is a browser component with an icon button, a results list and a polite live region.
Results appear as you type and the whole commodity list ships with the page; no server call is made.
The search runs on the server and lists nothing under 3 characters, because the real reference list is far larger than the stub.
DR1's live typing was rebuilt as a static server-rendered page, which cannot convey live typing.
The real search runs only on a Search button press, as a server round trip.

conflicts.outcome: Neither precedence nor DR1 settles it: the prototype wins by default, but it cannot express a page that works without JavaScript over a server-held reference list, and DR1 recorded the server-rendered rebuild only in passing, not as a ruling on the interaction. The default keeps both parts working.
conflicts.question: Should the real commodity search find results as you type in the browser, as DR2.1 does, or keep its server-side search behind the Search button?
conflicts.default: With JavaScript, the page behaves as DR2.1: results as you type from the server's commodity catalogue with no Search press, ticking keeps the results open, Escape closes them, and a live region announces result and selection counts. Without JavaScript, the page keeps today's server-side Search button, its 3-character minimum and the server-rendered panel, so it still works.

conflicts.about: The live-animals commodity search hint: DR2.1's common name / Latin name wording or the frontend's commodity name / species name wording with 'Enter at least 3 characters.'

positions.says: The hint reads 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).'
The hint reads 'You can search by commodity name (for example, Cow), commodity code (0102), or species name (Bos taurus). Enter at least 3 characters.'
Which wording ships is open and unruled, left to design and content.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1's wording is adopted. DR1 made no judgement (it left the hint open), so the prototype wins by default; the data reason DR1 recorded no longer holds, as common names are now searchable. The DR1 row stays as context, not overruled.

conflicts.about: Apparent data errors in DR2.1's species list: 'Equus cabalus' and 'Eq cabalus*asinus' for Equus caballus, and the near-duplicate 'Other mammalia' / 'Other Mammalia'.

positions.says: Horse species are 'Eq cabalus*asinus', 'Equus asinus' and 'Equus cabalus'.
Other live mammals holds both 'Other mammalia' and 'Other Mammalia', each 'Other mammal'.
The horse species renders 'Equus cabalus' though its id is equus-caballus, so the name looks misspelt.
The real service names the horse species 'Equus caballus'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, but its own id spells the name correctly, so whether the label is a design choice or a typo cannot be told from the sources; no DR1 judgement covers it.
conflicts.question: Should the real catalogue copy DR2.1's species spellings and its near-duplicate 'Other mammalia' entry as they are, or correct them?
conflicts.default: Correct them: 'Equus caballus' and 'Eq caballus*asinus', and one 'Other Mammalia (Other mammal)' entry; every other species name, common name and code exactly as DR2.1 gives it.

conflicts.about: How the commodity pages chain: as steps of the journey (DR2.1: back to the previous page, Save and continue to the next step) or with Commodity details as its own overview task (today: back to the overview, Save and continue to the overview).

positions.says: Commodity details' back link falls back to the commodity page.
The commodity page's back link goes to the origin page.
Save and continue on Commodity details goes to identification, additional or arrival details.
Commodity details is its own overview task, so its back link returns to the overview.
The commodity page's back link returns to the overview.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1's journey chaining is adopted: the prototype outranks the frontend's own design choice and no DR1 judgement covers it. repo-frontend-p5-038 and -p5-075 are not overruled, because they also record behaviour that stays (Save and return to overview going to the overview, packages stored only where they apply).

conflicts.about: Whether Commodity details ends with the three return controls: DR1's application of rule (b) listed it among the primary-button-only pages; DR2.1 and today give it all three.

positions.says: Rule (b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls.
Under inc-161, consignment details ends with the primary button alone.
Commodity details uses the shared journey actions: Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview.
Commodity details ends with all three controls now the hub links straight to it.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's rule (b), the highest-ranked judgement, is followed. In DR2.1 the overview's task list links to both the commodity page and Commodity details, so rule (b) gives both the three controls. DR1's page list applied the rule to DR1's journey, where consignment details was reached from another page; it is not overruled, because it ranks above the prototype, and the rule itself is what governs.

conflicts.about: The 'Error: ' browser title prefix on an error state: DR2.1 leaves it out; the real service adds it.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation, overrides the prototype.
In the commodity page's error state the title has no 'Error: ' prefix.
On Commodity details the title stays unchanged on a validation error.
The real commodity page prefixes its title 'Error: ' on an error.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the GOV.UK error pattern is part of the real validation the prototype does not model, so the 'Error: ' prefix stays.

conflicts.about: Opening Commodity details, or later pages, with no commodity chosen: DR2.1's guards never redirect; the real page sends the trader to the commodity page.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence or validation, overrides the prototype.
The consignment details and identifier guards do nothing.
The no-commodity guard never redirects, so later pages open with no commodity.
With no commodity lines, Commodity details redirects to the commodity page.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the prototype's guards are stubs, not a design, and a real notification cannot hold quantities for commodities it does not have, so the redirect stays.

conflicts.about: Validation of the live-animal number of packages: DR2.1 accepts any value; the real page accepts blank or a whole number of 1 or more.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation, overrides the prototype.
The live-animal packages field is not validated and may hold any value.
Packages are optional, but when given must be a whole number of at least 1, otherwise 'Number of packages must be a whole number, like 5'.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the field stays optional as DR2.1 has it, but the real service validates what it stores. The optional part of DR2.1 is still cited through prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-023 and trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-013.

conflicts.about: Cat and Dog species names: 'Domestic cat (Felis catus)' and 'Domestic dog (Canis familiaris)' (DR2.1) or 'Cat (Felis catus)' and 'Dog (Canis lupus familiaris)' (today).

positions.says: Cat's species is Felis catus, common name Domestic cat.
Dog's species is Canis familiaris, common name Domestic dog.
Whether Cat and Dog take the common names Domestic cat and Domestic dog is open and unruled.
The code search offers 'Cat (Felis catus)' and 'Dog (Canis lupus familiaris)'.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1's names are adopted: DR1 left the question unruled, so it is no judgement, and the prototype wins by default.

conflicts.about: Where a valid Save and continue on Commodity details goes after a change from check answers: DR2.1's commodity page returns to check answers, but its Commodity details drops the review origin and walks on.

positions.says: Commodity details keeps only a hub origin, so after a change from check answers Save and continue goes on to the next step.
The commodity page returns to the hub, review or template review as the entry point dictates.
The change context (?change=1) is kept through the commodity pages.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 contradicts itself between two adjacent pages, so precedence cannot settle it.
conflicts.question: After a trader changes commodity details from check answers, should Save and continue take them back to check answers, as DR2.1's commodity page does, or on to the next step, as DR2.1's Commodity details does?
conflicts.default: Back to check answers, from both pages, using the real service's change context; from the overview it returns to the overview, and while editing a template from its review it returns to the template.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal 'Total gross weight' is a gross or a net weight: DR2.1 labels it gross weight but stores it as netWeight.

positions.says: The field is labelled 'Total gross weight' but stored and validated as netWeight.
The weight is submitted as netWeight[<species>], so gross and net weight are conflated.

conflicts.outcome: DR2.1 contradicts itself, and the two readings store different quantities in the notification record the backend keeps and passes on.
conflicts.question: Is the germinal products weight the consignment's gross weight, as the label says, or its net weight, as DR2.1 stores it?
conflicts.default: Gross weight: the label 'Total gross weight' is kept and the answer is stored and passed on as the gross weight, per species.
